sections.title: The letter zê
paragraphs: The letter is called (zê) /ze/. Its main sound is heard in (zebra) /ˈze.βɾɐ/, an animal with stripes. The letter makes three sounds.

sections.title: Mouth and voice
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your tongue close to the tooth ridge. Push air through the narrow gap with your voice on. Touch your throat to feel it buzz. For the second sound, pull your tongue slightly back and round your lips softly. Push air through with no voice. For the third sound, keep the same mouth position, but turn your voice on.

sections.title: Where each sound occurs
paragraphs: At the start of a word or between vowels, it sounds like (fazer) /fɐˈzeɾ/. At the end of a word before a pause or a voiceless consonant, it sounds like (paz) /paʃ/ and (luz clara) /luʃ ˈkla.ɾɐ/. A voiceless consonant is a sound made with your voice off. Before a voiced consonant, it sounds like (luz divina) /luʒ diˈvi.nɐ/ and (dez meses) /dɛʒ ˈmɛ.zɨʃ/.

sections.title: Common English mistakes
paragraphs: At the end of words, you might want to buzz like the s in please. Do not buzz at the end of a word before a pause. Use the soft sh sound in ship instead. When a voiced sound follows, make the gentle sound of s in treasure.
